segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “my heart often sickened at the work of my hands” slowly and put it in my own words: Alone on a remote Orkney island, Victor says his heart often sickened at the work of his hands. Next, craft. I notice the physical reaction, a sickened heart, to moral horror at what his hands are doing. The strongest word is “sickened”: it shows disgust rising in him as he repeats the act that ruined his life. Then, effect. Why does Victor's heart sicken as he builds the female creature? My answer: Victor now knows what his science can cause; his growing revulsion leads to his decision to destroy the female, which will bring the creature's revenge on Clerval and Elizabeth.
